correctness.rationale: The proof applies the verified exact Ghosh--Kumar angle formula twice. Maximality of the first factor implies its relative unitary H is Hadamard, so |H|^{circ 2} circ H=(1/m)H. The Kronecker defect then factors exactly as Q_{mn}(H tensor W)=(1/m)H tensor Q_n(W). Since H is unitary, operator norm multiplicativity gives the exact cosine factor (n-1)/(mn-1). Quantifiers, dimensions, normalized-trace setting, and the zero/maximal boundary cases are explicitly covered; no finite experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: The theorem answers a natural tensorial-behavior question for a newly explicit invariant: it gives an exact law when one factor pair is orthogonal, shows that a single maximally angled factor does not force a maximally angled product, and supplies a dimension-controlled tensor orthogonalization mechanism. This is structurally complementary to the known common-factor stability theorem and is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a mere numerical recomputation.
